title: Only capital that is presently deployable counts as Risk Capital — in-flight assets and uncodified commitments are excluded
content:
A.3.2.1.2.1 defines Total Risk Capital as "capital that is currently eligible, available, and verifiably under the Prime's control," and adds the operative test: "it must be currently deployable towards covering its Required Risk Capital obligations."

Two exclusions follow and both bite in ordinary operation. "In-flight capital (e.g., assets being bridged) does not contribute towards a Prime's TRC" — so an Agent moving capital between chains has a temporary hole in its coverage, and must either pre-fund or accept the gap. And commitments for future capital, including rental Accords for Prime-External or Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital "that have been agreed upon by counterparties but are not yet formally codified within the Atlas, cannot contribute towards a Prime's TRC until such formalization is complete."

The principle is that risk capital is only real if it can absorb a loss *at the moment the loss happens*. A loss event does not wait for a bridge to finalize or for a governance process to ratify an agreement, so anything that is merely promised or merely in transit is treated as absent.

This makes the definition adversarial rather than accounting-based. The obvious way to appear well-capitalized is to count committed capital, and the obvious way to be genuinely well-capitalized is to hold it — A.3.2.1.2.1 refuses the first. A.3.2.1.2 supplies the consequence: "Prime Agents must maintain at all times a level of TRC that exceeds their Aggregate RRC or be subject to penalties," with "at all times" ruling out period-end window dressing.

The cost is capital inefficiency at exactly the awkward moments — cross-chain rebalancing and onboarding new capital providers both require the Agent to be over-capitalized during the transition.
description: Total Risk Capital must be eligible, available and verifiably controlled; bridging assets and agreed-but-not-yet-Atlas-codified rental Accords contribute nothing until formalization completes.
